1.w: When you sit down to eat with a ruler, discern carefully what is before your face,

2.w: and put a knife to your throat if you are an owner of an appetite.

3.w: You should not mark out his delicacies, for it is bread of lies.

4.w: Do not toil to become rich, cease from your own understanding.

5.w: Will you make your eyes fly onto it, and it is not there? For it certainly makes for itself wings like an eagle [and] flies away [to] the heavens!

6.w: Do not eat the bread of one evil of eye, and do not mark out his delicacies.

7.w: For like one who calculates in his soul, so [is] he—“Eat and drink,” he says to you, and his heart [is] not with you.

8.w: Your morsel [that] you have eaten, you will vomit it up, and you will ruin your pleasant words!

9.w: Do not speak in the ears of a fool, for he will despise the wisdom of your words.

10.w: Do not remove a boundary of old, and do not enter into the fields of the fatherless.

11.w: For their Redeemer [is] strong—He will contend their dispute against you.

12.w: You must bring your heart to discipline, and your ears to the words of knowledge.

13.w: Do not withhold discipline from a child; if you strike him with the rod, he will not die.

14.w: You strike him with the rod, and you will deliver his soul from Sheol.

15.w: My son, if your heart is wise, my heart will be glad—even I.

16.w: And my kidneys will exult at the speaking of uprightness [by] your lips.

17.w: Do not let your heart be jealous of the sinners, but rather in the fear of YHWH all the day.

18.w: For surely there is a posterity, and your hope will not be cut off.

19.w: Listen you, my son, and be wise, and let your heart walk straight in the way.

20.w: Not Be among those getting drunk [on] wine, among those being gluttons of flesh to themelves.

21.w: For the drunkard and the glutton will be dispossessed, and drowsiness will clothe [them] in rags.

22.w: Listen to your father, this one begot you, and do not despise your mother when she is old.

23.w: Acquire truth and do not sell [it]—wisdom, and discipline, and discernment.

24.w: The father of a righteous one will greatly rejoice, and the one begetting a wise [son] will be glad in him.

25.w: Let your father and your mother be glad, and let she who bore you rejoice.

26.w: My son, give your heart to me, and let your eyes delight [in] my ways.

27.w: For a prostitute [is] a deep pit, and a strange woman [is] a narrow well.

28.w: She also, like a robber, lies in wait, and she increases the treacherous ones among men.

29.w: To whom [is] woe? To whom [is] sorrow? To whom [are] quarrels? To whom [is] complaining? To whom [are] wounds without cause? To whom [is] dullness of eyes?

30.w: To those lingering over the wine, to those going in search of mixed drink!

31.w: Do not look [at] the wine when it is red, when it gives forth its eye in the cup—it goes down with smoothness!

32.w: Its end [is] like a serpent—it bites, and like a viper it stings.

33.w: Your eyes will see strange things, and your heart will speak perverse things.

34.w: And you will become like one lying down in the heart of the sea, and like one lying down on the top of a mast:

35.w: “They struck me; I did not become weak. They beat me; I did not know [it]. When I awake, I will add to seek it again?”
